## Natural history notes

A large earwig characterized by its elongated tan to reddish-brown body, long antennae, short wings, and prominent curved forceps at the tip of the abdomen. In Florida, it is found in sandy or moist open habitats such as beaches, shorelines, riverbanks, marsh edges, fields, gardens, and disturbed areas where it can hide under debris, stones, logs, or leaf litter. It is an opportunistic predator and scavenger, feeding on small insects, eggs, carrion, and organic matter, and is most active at night while sheltering in concealed places during the day.
